title: How to Carve the Perfect Halloween Pumpkin
paragraphs: Carving pumpkins is one of the most popular Halloween activities. Carved pumpkins with faces or patterns and a light inside are called jack-o'-lanterns. If you want to make a great one, here are some useful tips.

First, choose the right pumpkin. Look for one that is fresh and firm, with no damaged spots. It should also have a flat bottom, so it can stand without rolling over. Bigger pumpkins are often easier to carve than small ones.
Be careful when you carry your pumpkin. Lift it from underneath instead of holding it by the stem. If you hold it by the stem, the stem might break off.
Before you start carving, make sure the pumpkin is sitting on a firm, flat surface so that it does not move around. This will make carving easier and safer.

It is also important to use the right tools. Some people find that a knife with a serrated edge, like a steak knife, works well for cutting the pumpkin. For small, detailed designs, a very sharp craft knife can be useful.
When you carve your design, cut along the outline first. Then you can use a pointed tool to make the corners and edges look clean.
Timing is very important, too. A carved pumpkin does not last very long, so it is a good idea to carve it no more than three to five days before you want to show it.
Finally, think carefully about how to light it. A battery-powered candle is a safe choice, because it does not have a real flame.
With these tips, you can make a jack-o'-lantern that everyone will enjoy.
